description: How much of a Robinhood Chain token a market maker's trading wallet holds, and when that wallet first approved the token, read from the chain. An approval is a transaction in which a wallet gives a contract permission to move its holdings of one token. A market maker makes one when it is getting ready to trade a token, which can be before an exchange lists the token: Wintermute's trading contract first approved Cash Cat on August 5, 2026, and Robinhood listed that token on August 6, 2026. A first approval is a lead to look into: it does not say why the market maker wants the token, and it does not mean an exchange will list it. Pass the token's contract address as `token`; the `contract` of an entry from brainchain_custody_additions works. `token` can also be a symbol or name, such as RLUSD or Ripple USD, looked up on BitGo's lists for Robinhood Chain; when none there goes by it, on the lists the BrainChain MCP dataset records (Trust Wallet, MetaMask, LI.FI, CoinGecko, KuCoin and Gate); and when none there does either, among every token with a Uniswap pool by the symbol its contract gives itself (`pool index`). When exactly one token goes by it, `lookup` in the answer names the `contract` it stands for and its `source`, and for one found in the dataset the `dataset` day, block and manifest read; when several do, the answer lists them as `candidates`, each with its `source`, and reads nothing more. A symbol is whatever the token's deployer chose, so check the contract before relying on one found in the pool index. The tool follows five wallets at three firms: Wintermute's trading contract at 0x51C72848c68a965f66FA7a88855F9f7784502a7F, two more Wintermute wallets, one B2C2 wallet and one Galaxy Digital wallet. Etherscan tags the contract's address as a market maker and Arkham attributes it to Wintermute. The other four are plain wallets with a public name tag on Etherscan, which each entry repeats as `tag`. To read another wallet instead, pass its address as `wallet`. Unless it is one of the five, its entry has no `name` or `tag`, and the tool does not check whose wallet it is. In the answer, `token` holds the token's `contract`, the `name` and `symbol` the contract gives itself, its `decimals` and its `totalSupply`, counted in tokens and not in the token's smallest unit. Whoever deployed the contract chose the name and symbol, so they do not prove which token it is. `wallets` has one entry for each wallet read: the `wallet`, the firm's `name`, the `tag`, the `balance` it holds now, also counted in tokens, and `shareOfSupplyPct`, that balance as a percentage of the total supply, which is left out for a token with no supply. `firstApproval` is there only if the token's log shows an approval by the wallet: `at` is when, `block` is the block it is in, `spender` is the contract it gave permission to, and `transaction` is the transaction's hash. `confirmed` is true when the wallet took part in that transaction: the wallet sent it, it was sent to the wallet or, for Wintermute's trading contract, it was sent to the Safe at 0x7d330DD7AF628c24E9FC75eb2986b130b2125ad0. Every approval of the Cash Cat and Pons tokens by that contract has gone through that Safe. When `confirmed` is false, the token's own log is the only sign of the approval. A token's contract writes its own balances and logs, so whoever deployed a token can make any wallet appear to hold it or to have approved it, and anyone can send a wallet tokens. For a token whose origin you do not know, a `balance` therefore proves little, and a `firstApproval` counts only when its `confirmed` is true. A wallet with a zero `balance` and no `firstApproval` holds none of the token now and has never approved it. A market maker also trades from other wallets, so that does not mean the firm holds none. `readAt` is when the chain was read. Without `atBlock` or `at`, each `balance` is what the wallet holds at `block`, the newest block when the chain was read, and the entry is marked `currentOnly`: it shows nothing of what could be seen earlier, so leave it out of a backtest. To read the balances at a past block, pass its number as `atBlock`, or pass `at`, a time in ISO 8601 such as 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z, for the last block made at or before it. Robinhood Chain's public endpoint keeps no state that old, so the tool adds up the token's Transfer logs to and from each wallet up to that block. It checks the method at the newest block, where the same sum must equal what the token's own `balanceOf` says. `asOf` then gives the `block` asked for and when it was made (`at`), and `transfersCheck` gives the `block` checked and whether the check `passed`. If it did not, the token's balances do not follow its transfers, as with a token that rebases or takes a fee on each transfer, and no past `balance` is given: `transfersCheck` names the first `wallet` that differs, what its `transfers` add up to and what `balanceOf` says. A past entry has no `shareOfSupplyPct`, since the supply at that block is not read, and `token` is read at the newest block. `firstApproval` is the first approval whenever it was made, so compare its `block` with the one asked for. The tool answers one request at a time, so requests sent together are answered in turn. The first answer for a token can take half a minute, because the tool reads the token's whole history for each wallet; later ones are faster for as long as the server keeps running. At a past block it also reads every transfer of the token to and from each wallet, which can take several tries for a wallet that trades the token often. An answer that is not ready after 45 seconds says so, and asking again goes on from where it stopped. Free, no key and no payment. Not advice.

at.description: Optional, in place of atBlock: a time in ISO 8601, such as 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z. The balances are those at the last block made at or before it.

atBlock.description: Optional: a block number. The balances are those at the end of that block, added up from the token's transfers.

token.description: The token's contract address on Robinhood Chain, 0x followed by 40 hex characters, or its symbol or name, such as RLUSD.

wallet.description: Optional: the address of another wallet or contract to read instead of the wallets the tool follows.

name: brainchain_market_maker_holdings
title: A market maker's holdings and first approval of a Robinhood Chain token
